title: Storage — Extract pure semantic-state rules from persistence with compatibility parity
body:
## Problem and intended outcome

State meaning and storage mechanics currently share modules. Separate a small, demonstrably pure rule boundary so that a change to semantic validation or fingerprint construction can be reviewed and checked without SQL, while the existing operation owner retains atomicity and authorization.

Coordination: #1209. The active architecture/protocol owner remains [02](https://github.com/hynk-studio/augnes/blob/52f8b278bad5ddd8c261af127dca712cdd8da925/docs/vnext/02_AUGNES_VNEXT_ARCHITECTURE_AND_PROTOCOL.md). Suggested implementation order: **3**.

## Current source evidence

Source audit baseline: [`52f8b278bad5ddd8c261af127dca712cdd8da925`](https://github.com/hynk-studio/augnes/commit/52f8b278bad5ddd8c261af127dca712cdd8da925), rechecked on 2026-10-10 KST. The source findings below were inspected through GitHub; this registration did not reproduce runtime failures or run Local Canonical. Main integration is distinct from installed-runtime adoption.

- [durable-semantic-store.ts](https://github.com/hynk-studio/augnes/blob/52f8b278bad5ddd8c261af127dca712cdd8da925/lib/vnext/persistence/durable-semantic-store.ts#L746-L906) includes candidate/target matching, semantic-state construction, identity/fingerprint calculation and validation alongside SQL persistence APIs in the same file.
- [lib/db.ts](https://github.com/hynk-studio/augnes/blob/52f8b278bad5ddd8c261af127dca712cdd8da925/lib/db.ts#L469-L482) invokes `scoreCandidateProposal()` from a persistence flow.
- Both files have the same Git blob identities as the prior reviewed `d2d1d14` baseline. This is unchanged responsibility coupling, not a newly reproduced runtime failure or an argument based only on file length.

## Proposed first slice

Audit consumers and choose the smallest existing set of DB-independent semantic-state construction/normalization/validation/fingerprint rules to extract. Keep compatibility exports where they avoid unnecessary caller churn. The source functions above are investigation leads; current contracts determine the actual boundary.

The desired dependency direction is:

- Pure rules depend on protocol/types and deterministic primitives.
- Persistence owns SQL, representation and indexed record access.
- The existing operation coordinator owns current-state/authority rechecks and the complete transaction.

Audit the legacy scoring call and research/compatibility imports to identify later separable responsibilities, but do not combine unrelated scoring-policy or historical-code cleanup with the first extraction.

## Acceptance and invariants

- [x] A caller inventory identifies runtime, recovery, compatibility and test consumers of the extracted rules.
- [x] The extracted rule module needs no database connection or schema preparation, and its dependencies do not pull persistence back into the pure boundary.
- [x] Representative existing persisted fixtures reconstruct to identical semantic content, record IDs, fingerprints and externally observable validation results.
- [x] Invalid candidate/target relationships, wrong project scope, tampered fingerprints and malformed required state still refuse.
- [x] Actual writer paths preserve exact replay, altered replay/stale-state refusal, review-versus-apply separation and atomic rollback.
- [x] Transaction ownership remains with the existing complete operation; extraction does not introduce nested independent commits or storage functions that silently commit.
- [x] Existing exports/callers remain compatible or migrate in a bounded reviewed change; show the before/after dependency boundary and any remaining coupling.

Do not change schema, serialized records, hashing/canonicalization semantics, execution authority or stored historical meaning. Do not delete research/compatibility material or introduce a new framework merely to make modules smaller.

## Verification and status

**Completed by #1444, merged on 2026-10-12 at 03:34:39 KST (`2026-10-11T18:34:39Z`).** The issue was already `closed` with reason `completed` when this post-merge reconciliation was performed. This update records the seven satisfied acceptance criteria and replaces the obsolete not-started status; it does not perform another merge or issue-state transition. The original problem, source baseline and intended scope above remain historical context.

### Integrated identity

- Verified pre-merge base: `8712203e06c951ce52044d784c75da4d61078fbd`.
- Verified PR head: `0eac7b546fd77c6a2146c5e75b1256d7a49976f0`.
- Merge commit and freshly observed `main`: `a36f96676aa88e6def5218b8ae63698f36e6295b`.
- Both the PR head and merged `main` have Git tree `0eb6d3ab4bda0f4e1dccdba0058b1fda5b2d6ec1`; the merge parents are the verified base and head. Post-merge GitHub reads therefore show no tracked-content divergence from the reviewed candidate.

### Acceptance evidence

Implementation, caller inventory, exact development commands, preserved setup failures and deciding results are recorded in [PR #1444](https://github.com/hynk-studio/augnes/pull/1444).

| Criterion | Recorded evidence |
|---|---|
| Caller inventory | 17 direct state-rule consumers across runtime writers, projections, recovery/portability, compatibility and tests; candidate-hash consumers and the legacy scoring call were also audited. |
| DB-independent boundary | `semantic-state-rules.ts` and `episode-delta-candidate.ts`; non-tree-shaken dependency audit and restricted execution cover eight runtime modules with only `node:crypto.createHash` externally. No persistence back-import, DB or schema preparation is required. |
| Persisted-data parity | Frozen pre-extraction generic, Claim and Claim–Evidence relation fixtures compare construction/reconstruction, exact IDs, target keys, fingerprints and observable validation results. |
| Refusal parity | 64 baseline-captured refusals compare names/messages, codes/paths where present, complete validation results and first-error ordering. |
| Actual writer safety | Real writer, lifecycle, fresh-session and recovery coverage preserves exact/altered replay, stale-state and authority refusal, review/apply separation and complete ledger/projection/head rollback checks. |
| Complete operation ownership | No coordinator, transaction, SQL or schema behavior changed; no nested independent commit or silently committing helper was introduced. |
| Compatibility and remaining coupling | Existing exports, function/error-constructor identity and cross-path `instanceof` are preserved. SQL/indexed access, broader compatibility orchestration and legacy scoring policy remain deliberately outside this extraction. |

### Evidence and authority limits

The receipt remains evidence for the exact **pre-merge head**, not a newly executed validation of the merge commit. Matching Git trees is a separate post-merge source-identity observation. This reconciliation did not rerun tests or the Mac receipt validator and does not claim independent execution attestation.

Source integration is complete. Installed-runtime adoption, installation, production migration/writes, provider experiments, deployment and measured productivity/live-model usefulness are not established by this closure. The implementation report preserves the installed Companion identity and production state; this metadata-only reconciliation did not inspect or modify that local runtime. No PR monitoring or scheduled verification was created.
